top_news.title: She Starts
top_news.summary: VMPL New Delhi [India], October 12: As artificial intelligence reshapes workplace expectations, women returning to employment after career breaks are increasingly exploring AI-integrated learning to rebuild their professional capabilities. With AI literacy, digital collaboration and practical technology skills becoming relevant across industries, conventional upskilling alone may no longer adequately prepare career returners for today's workplace. AI also presents an opportunity to narrow the skills gap. As both experienced professionals and returning candidates adapt to emerging technologies, women re-entering the workforce have an opportunity to develop capabilities aligned with current employer expectations. Against this backdrop, She Starts, a remote-first career restart platform, is reporting growing interest in its AI-integrated programmes, which combine practical learning, recent workplace experience and structured career preparation. She Starts Supports Over 500 Women She Starts has already supported more than 500 women through its career restart ecosystem, extending its reach globally through a hiring network of 300+ across 25+ countries. Its participants include women returning after motherhood, caregiving responsibilities, relocation and extended career breaks, ranging from those seeking to resume previous careers to others exploring new professional opportunities. Participation in AI-integrated career restart programmes is gaining momentum as women recognise the importance of developing current workplace capabilities alongside their existing qualifications and experience, while addressing challenges associated with employment gaps. Increasing participation among Indian expatriate women also highlights the growing interest in flexible learning and location-independent career pathways among those living outside their home countries. Rather than focusing exclusively on certifications, She Starts aims to address the broader challenges of career re-entry through practical learning, recent professional experience, confidence rebuilding and structured employment preparation. 40+ AI-Integrated Programmes Across Different Career Domains At the centre of She Starts' approach is the integration of artificial intelligence into professional learning, helping participants understand how emerging technologies are applied in everyday workplace activities. Its portfolio spans 40+ career restart-friendly courses across different domains: Business and Operations, Marketing and Creative, Data and Technology, and Life Sciences and Education. The approach reflects the expanding application of AI across industries, from administrative coordination and business communication to marketing, content development, data analysis and knowledge-based work. In business operations, AI tools can support documentation, information management and workflow coordination. Marketing and creative professionals increasingly use AI-assisted processes for content planning, research and production, while data-oriented roles require familiarity with AI-supported analysis and interpretation. She Starts combines career-focused learning with hands-on assignments, practical projects and portfolio development, helping women demonstrate relevant capabilities rather than relying solely on previous employment experience. These skills are particularly relevant to remote and hybrid workplaces, where digital proficiency, independent execution and effective online collaboration are increasingly important. Beyond Upskilling: Bridging Career Gaps Through Recent Workplace Experience For women returning after extended career breaks, acquiring new skills is only part of the challenge. Despite possessing relevant qualifications and previous professional experience, many face the additional challenge of demonstrating recent workplace capabilities and familiarity with current employer expectations. Recognising this gap, She Starts integrates on-the-job training (OJT) opportunities into its career restart ecosystem, enabling participants to apply newly acquired skills in practical working environments, develop credible portfolios and gain recent, relevant experience that can strengthen their professional profiles. While such experience does not erase an earlier career break, it can provide employers with additional evidence of a candidate's current capabilities and readiness to re-enter the workforce. This approach forms part of She Starts' Career Restart Operating System (CROS), structured around three stages: Reset, Rebuild and Restart. Alongside AI-integrated learning, the platform provides career coaching, OJT, professional branding, interview preparation and placement readiness support for remote and work-from-home opportunities. Delivered by an all-women training team, the model connects updated skills with practical experience and professional confidence, positioning career re-entry as a structured transition rather than an exercise limited to course completion. Bangalore Office Strengthens Indian Operations She Starts, operating globally from the UK, has expanded its Indian operational presence through a virtual office in Bangalore under its parent company, Zylenverse Private Limited. The development supports programme coordination, institutional engagement and the organisation's wider plans for the Indian market. Bangalore's established technology and business ecosystem provides a relevant operational base for an organisation focused on AI-integrated professional development and remote career pathways. While programme delivery remains remote-first, allowing participants to access learning opportunities without relocating, the additional presence strengthens She Starts' ability to coordinate activities and expand engagement across Indian cities. Career Restart Conclaves Expand Beyond Digital Learning Alongside its online programmes, She Starts is building an in-person engagement network through its Career Restart Conclaves. The organisation has conducted two conclaves, in Calicut and Bangalore, featuring career conversations, AI-focused workshops, networking opportunities and a work-from-home job fair. The events reflect She Starts' recognition that career re-entry involves more than acquiring new skills. Professional networking, confidence rebuilding, awareness of changing employment expectations and community engagement also play important roles in helping women return to professional life. Following the Bangalore conclave, She Starts is preparing its next Career Restart Conclave in Cochin, with plans to organise monthly events across Tier 1 and Tier 2 Indian cities. The proposed expansion aims to connect the organisation's remote learning ecosystem with physical community engagement, creating additional opportunities for women to explore AI-enabled career pathways and professional development. GCC Participation Drives Plans for UAE Expansion Women based in GCC countries account for a significant share of She Starts' participant base, making the region an important market for its remote-first career restart programmes. Flexible learning and location-independent career preparation are particularly relevant to women managing relocation, caregiving responsibilities and career interruptions while living abroad. To strengthen its regional presence, She Starts is planning to establish an office in the United Arab Emirates. The proposed expansion would support programme operations, community engagement and future employer partnerships across the GCC, while strengthening connections between the organisation's Indian and international activities. Founders Highlight the Importance of AI Skills and Recent Experience Dr. Arun Mohan, Co-Founder of She Starts, believes AI-integrated learning and recent professional experience are becoming increasingly important for career returners. "AI is changing the skills expected of almost every professional, creating an opportunity for women returning after a career break. But learning new skills alone is not enough. Employers also need evidence that candidates can apply those skills in real working environments. Combining AI-integrated learning with recent on-the-job experience can help women demonstrate their capabilities and rebuild professional credibility. The focus should be on what they can contribute now, rather than allowing the duration of their career break to define their professional potential." Noble Mathew, Co-Founder of She Starts, emphasises the importance of practical experience and professional confidence. "Learning new skills is only one part of returning to work. Women also need opportunities to apply their knowledge, build credible portfolios and rebuild their professional identity. Practical assignments and on-the-job experience can help demonstrate current capabilities to employers. Our focus is on connecting learning with genuine workplace readiness while helping women rebuild confidence in their professional identity." The Road Ahead She Starts plans to expand its AI-integrated career pathways, continue its Career Restart Conclaves across India and strengthen employer partnerships across the globe. As artificial intelligence transforms professional roles, structured career restart initiatives combining contemporary skills with practical workplace experience could help more women navigate career breaks and return to professional employment. About She Starts She Starts is a remote-first, AI-integrated career restart ecosystem supporting women returning after career breaks. Its Career Restart Operating System combines practical learning, career coaching, OJT opportunities where available, portfolio development, professional branding and placement readiness to prepare women for remote and hybrid careers. More information about She Starts and its programmes is available at www.shestarts.online. (ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL. ANI will not be responsible in any way for the content of the same.)

top_news.title: T-MAXIMUM
top_news.summary: BEIJING, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- T-MAXIMUM PHARMACEUTICAL ("T-MAXIMUM") today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the company to initiate a Phase 2 clinical study of MT027, its internally developed, B7-H3-targeted universal (allogeneic) CAR-T therapy, for the treatment of patients with brain metastases from lung cancer and breast cancer. This is the second Phase 2 study of MT027 to receive FDA clearance. MT027 was previously cleared by the FDA to proceed with a Phase 2 study in recurrent glioblastoma, and has been granted Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) and Fast Track Designation (FTD). With two FDA-cleared Phase 2 programs, T-MAXIMUM has established a dual-indication portfolio for universal CAR-T therapy covering both primary and metastatic intracranial solid tumors. Image source: T-MAXIMUM official website (www.t-maximum.com) Brain Metastases: An Unanswered Clinical Question Despite Advances in Systemic Therapy Brain metastases commonly arise in patients with lung cancer, breast cancer, melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, and colorectal cancer. International studies estimate that approximately 20% of cancer patients may develop brain metastases over the course of their disease, a proportion that can reach 20% to 40% among patients with advanced solid tumors.[1][2] For patients, this means far more than an additional lesion on imaging: brain metastases may be accompanied by headaches, seizures, and cognitive and motor impairment, directly affecting daily life and subsequent treatment options. This is a truly global clinical challenge. In 2022, there were nearly 20 million new cancer cases worldwide, including nearly 2.5 million new cases of lung cancer and approximately 2.3 million new cases of female breast cancer - the two leading primary tumor types giving rise to brain metastases.[3] Asia accounts for roughly half of all new cancer cases globally;[4] in the United States, an estimated 200,000 to 300,000 patients are newly diagnosed with brain metastases each year.[2] This large patient population means brain metastasis is not a niche need, but a question that oncology worldwide must continue to answer. Systemic therapies can help control disease throughout the body, but treatment of intracranial lesions often remains constrained by multiple factors, including the blood-brain barrier, tumor heterogeneity, and the need to preserve neurological function. This is especially true for patients who experience intracranial progression after prior therapy, for whom there remains a need for more treatment options that are validated intracranially while balancing safety and accessibility. Consecutive Clinical Milestones Built on Long-Term Product and Translational Groundwork MT027's recent series of regulatory milestones is no coincidence. It reflects an integrated capability across product, manufacturing, clinical development, and regulatory affairs built around intracranial solid tumors - one that is now advancing from early exploration toward more systematic clinical validation. First, a foundation of clinical data. The company has accumulated sustained clinical experience in local delivery, repeat dosing, and safety monitoring for intracranial solid tumors. Years of clinical experience and data with MT027 have already led to two FDA-cleared Phase 2 programs. Data from an investigator-initiated trial (IIT) of MT026, a program built on the same platform, were published in Nature Communications in 2026: among 5 patients with recurrent high-grade glioma, 1 complete response and 3 partial responses were observed, for an objective response rate (ORR) of 80%, with no treatment-related Grade 3 or higher adverse events. Early clinical data for MT027 in patients with refractory brain metastases from lung cancer were previously presented at the IASLC 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC 2026). Five heavily pretreated patients with no guideline-recommended subsequent treatment options completed treatment; among the 3 evaluable patients, 2 partial responses were observed. The safety profile was favorable, with no Grade 3 or higher adverse events and no graft-versus-host disease (GvHD). These rigorous exploratory clinical studies provide an important basis for the clinical translation of allogeneic, locally delivered CAR-T therapy in intracranial solid tumors. Second, a well-defined manufacturing process. MT027 is manufactured using a fully non-viral gene-editing process - a generational departure from the industry's mainstream lentiviral vector approach - offering potential advantages in product safety, batch-to-batch consistency, and cost control. The manufacturing process was established and locked prior to entering Phase 2 clinical development. Third, leadership measured not only by getting there first, but by advancing systematically. For an innovative cell therapy company, leadership in regulatory progress comes from coordinated advancement across product, manufacturing, clinical development, and regulatory strategy. MT027's consecutive entry into FDA-cleared Phase 2 clinical development demonstrates T-MAXIMUM's ability to translate its prior groundwork into a repeatable and scalable clinical development capability. Management Commentary "Receiving FDA clearance for two consecutive Phase 2 studies of MT027 marks a pivotal step built on our sustained work in intracranial solid tumors. From glioma to brain metastases, we have always let the data speak and put clinical value first. Going forward, we will continue to rigorously evaluate the product's safety and potential clinical value through well-designed clinical studies, steadily advancing product supply, clinical execution, and the generation of key data, as we explore new possibilities for patients who lack effective treatment options." About MT027 MT027 is an investigational, B7-H3-targeted universal (allogeneic) CAR-T cell therapy developed by T-MAXIMUM using a fully non-viral gene-editing process and administered via local intracranial delivery. MT027 has received FDA Orphan Drug Designation and Fast Track Designation and is being evaluated in FDA-cleared Phase 2 studies in recurrent glioblastoma and in brain metastases from lung cancer and breast cancer. About T-MAXIMUM PHARMACEUTICAL T-MAXIMUM PHARMACEUTICAL is a clinical-stage cell therapy company focused on developing universal (allogeneic) CAR-T therapies for intracranial solid tumors with high unmet medical need, including recurrent glioblastoma and brain metastases. Through engineered cell therapies, local delivery strategies, and clinical translation capabilities, the Company is advancing more accessible treatment approaches with the potential to support repeat dosing. Its lead program, MT027, is a B7-H3-targeted universal CAR-T therapy that has received FDA clearance to initiate Phase 2 clinical studies in recurrent glioblastoma and brain metastases. MT027 has also received Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) in high-grade glioma and Fast Track Designation (FTD) for recurrent or progressive glioblastoma. T-MAXIMUM is working to translate its accumulated capabilities in product development, manufacturing, and clinical execution into continued innovation across both primary and metastatic intracranial solid tumors, with the goal of creating new possibilities for patients with limited treatment options. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements, including statements regarding the clinical development, potential therapeutic benefits, manufacturing advantages, and regulatory progress of MT027 and other product candidates. These statements are based on current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties, including those inherent in clinical development, regulatory review, and manufacturing, that could cause actual results to differ materially. Early clinical results from small numbers of patients may not be predictive of results in larger studies. MT027 is an investigational product, and its safety and efficacy have not been established. articles.title: She Starts
articles.summary: VMPL New Delhi [India], October 12: As artificial intelligence reshapes workplace expectations, women returning to employment after career breaks are increasingly exploring AI-integrated learning to rebuild their professional capabilities. With AI literacy, digital collaboration and practical technology skills becoming relevant across industries, conventional upskilling alone may no longer adequately prepare career returners for today's workplace. AI also presents an opportunity to narrow the skills gap. As both experienced professionals and returning candidates adapt to emerging technologies, women re-entering the workforce have an opportunity to develop capabilities aligned with current employer expectations. Against this backdrop, She Starts, a remote-first career restart platform, is reporting growing interest in its AI-integrated programmes, which combine practical learning, recent workplace experience and structured career preparation. She Starts Supports Over 500 Women She Starts has already supported more than 500 women through its career restart ecosystem, extending its reach globally through a hiring network of 300+ across 25+ countries. Its participants include women returning after motherhood, caregiving responsibilities, relocation and extended career breaks, ranging from those seeking to resume previous careers to others exploring new professional opportunities. Participation in AI-integrated career restart programmes is gaining momentum as women recognise the importance of developing current workplace capabilities alongside their existing qualifications and experience, while addressing challenges associated with employment gaps. Increasing participation among Indian expatriate women also highlights the growing interest in flexible learning and location-independent career pathways among those living outside their home countries. Rather than focusing exclusively on certifications, She Starts aims to address the broader challenges of career re-entry through practical learning, recent professional experience, confidence rebuilding and structured employment preparation. 40+ AI-Integrated Programmes Across Different Career Domains At the centre of She Starts' approach is the integration of artificial intelligence into professional learning, helping participants understand how emerging technologies are applied in everyday workplace activities. Its portfolio spans 40+ career restart-friendly courses across different domains: Business and Operations, Marketing and Creative, Data and Technology, and Life Sciences and Education. The approach reflects the expanding application of AI across industries, from administrative coordination and business communication to marketing, content development, data analysis and knowledge-based work. In business operations, AI tools can support documentation, information management and workflow coordination. Marketing and creative professionals increasingly use AI-assisted processes for content planning, research and production, while data-oriented roles require familiarity with AI-supported analysis and interpretation. She Starts combines career-focused learning with hands-on assignments, practical projects and portfolio development, helping women demonstrate relevant capabilities rather than relying solely on previous employment experience. These skills are particularly relevant to remote and hybrid workplaces, where digital proficiency, independent execution and effective online collaboration are increasingly important. Beyond Upskilling: Bridging Career Gaps Through Recent Workplace Experience For women returning after extended career breaks, acquiring new skills is only part of the challenge. Despite possessing relevant qualifications and previous professional experience, many face the additional challenge of demonstrating recent workplace capabilities and familiarity with current employer expectations. Recognising this gap, She Starts integrates on-the-job training (OJT) opportunities into its career restart ecosystem, enabling participants to apply newly acquired skills in practical working environments, develop credible portfolios and gain recent, relevant experience that can strengthen their professional profiles. While such experience does not erase an earlier career break, it can provide employers with additional evidence of a candidate's current capabilities and readiness to re-enter the workforce. This approach forms part of She Starts' Career Restart Operating System (CROS), structured around three stages: Reset, Rebuild and Restart. Alongside AI-integrated learning, the platform provides career coaching, OJT, professional branding, interview preparation and placement readiness support for remote and work-from-home opportunities. Delivered by an all-women training team, the model connects updated skills with practical experience and professional confidence, positioning career re-entry as a structured transition rather than an exercise limited to course completion. Bangalore Office Strengthens Indian Operations She Starts, operating globally from the UK, has expanded its Indian operational presence through a virtual office in Bangalore under its parent company, Zylenverse Private Limited. The development supports programme coordination, institutional engagement and the organisation's wider plans for the Indian market. Bangalore's established technology and business ecosystem provides a relevant operational base for an organisation focused on AI-integrated professional development and remote career pathways. While programme delivery remains remote-first, allowing participants to access learning opportunities without relocating, the additional presence strengthens She Starts' ability to coordinate activities and expand engagement across Indian cities. Career Restart Conclaves Expand Beyond Digital Learning Alongside its online programmes, She Starts is building an in-person engagement network through its Career Restart Conclaves. The organisation has conducted two conclaves, in Calicut and Bangalore, featuring career conversations, AI-focused workshops, networking opportunities and a work-from-home job fair. The events reflect She Starts' recognition that career re-entry involves more than acquiring new skills. Professional networking, confidence rebuilding, awareness of changing employment expectations and community engagement also play important roles in helping women return to professional life. Following the Bangalore conclave, She Starts is preparing its next Career Restart Conclave in Cochin, with plans to organise monthly events across Tier 1 and Tier 2 Indian cities. The proposed expansion aims to connect the organisation's remote learning ecosystem with physical community engagement, creating additional opportunities for women to explore AI-enabled career pathways and professional development. GCC Participation Drives Plans for UAE Expansion Women based in GCC countries account for a significant share of She Starts' participant base, making the region an important market for its remote-first career restart programmes. Flexible learning and location-independent career preparation are particularly relevant to women managing relocation, caregiving responsibilities and career interruptions while living abroad. To strengthen its regional presence, She Starts is planning to establish an office in the United Arab Emirates. The proposed expansion would support programme operations, community engagement and future employer partnerships across the GCC, while strengthening connections between the organisation's Indian and international activities. Founders Highlight the Importance of AI Skills and Recent Experience Dr. Arun Mohan, Co-Founder of She Starts, believes AI-integrated learning and recent professional experience are becoming increasingly important for career returners. "AI is changing the skills expected of almost every professional, creating an opportunity for women returning after a career break. But learning new skills alone is not enough. Employers also need evidence that candidates can apply those skills in real working environments. Combining AI-integrated learning with recent on-the-job experience can help women demonstrate their capabilities and rebuild professional credibility. The focus should be on what they can contribute now, rather than allowing the duration of their career break to define their professional potential." Noble Mathew, Co-Founder of She Starts, emphasises the importance of practical experience and professional confidence. "Learning new skills is only one part of returning to work. Women also need opportunities to apply their knowledge, build credible portfolios and rebuild their professional identity. Practical assignments and on-the-job experience can help demonstrate current capabilities to employers. Our focus is on connecting learning with genuine workplace readiness while helping women rebuild confidence in their professional identity." The Road Ahead She Starts plans to expand its AI-integrated career pathways, continue its Career Restart Conclaves across India and strengthen employer partnerships across the globe. As artificial intelligence transforms professional roles, structured career restart initiatives combining contemporary skills with practical workplace experience could help more women navigate career breaks and return to professional employment. About She Starts She Starts is a remote-first, AI-integrated career restart ecosystem supporting women returning after career breaks. Its Career Restart Operating System combines practical learning, career coaching, OJT opportunities where available, portfolio development, professional branding and placement readiness to prepare women for remote and hybrid careers. More information about She Starts and its programmes is available at www.shestarts.online. (ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL. ANI will not be responsible in any way for the content of the same.)

articles.title: T-MAXIMUM
articles.summary: BEIJING, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- T-MAXIMUM PHARMACEUTICAL ("T-MAXIMUM") today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the company to initiate a Phase 2 clinical study of MT027, its internally developed, B7-H3-targeted universal (allogeneic) CAR-T therapy, for the treatment of patients with brain metastases from lung cancer and breast cancer. This is the second Phase 2 study of MT027 to receive FDA clearance. MT027 was previously cleared by the FDA to proceed with a Phase 2 study in recurrent glioblastoma, and has been granted Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) and Fast Track Designation (FTD). With two FDA-cleared Phase 2 programs, T-MAXIMUM has established a dual-indication portfolio for universal CAR-T therapy covering both primary and metastatic intracranial solid tumors. Image source: T-MAXIMUM official website (www.t-maximum.com) Brain Metastases: An Unanswered Clinical Question Despite Advances in Systemic Therapy Brain metastases commonly arise in patients with lung cancer, breast cancer, melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, and colorectal cancer. International studies estimate that approximately 20% of cancer patients may develop brain metastases over the course of their disease, a proportion that can reach 20% to 40% among patients with advanced solid tumors.[1][2] For patients, this means far more than an additional lesion on imaging: brain metastases may be accompanied by headaches, seizures, and cognitive and motor impairment, directly affecting daily life and subsequent treatment options. This is a truly global clinical challenge. In 2022, there were nearly 20 million new cancer cases worldwide, including nearly 2.5 million new cases of lung cancer and approximately 2.3 million new cases of female breast cancer - the two leading primary tumor types giving rise to brain metastases.[3] Asia accounts for roughly half of all new cancer cases globally;[4] in the United States, an estimated 200,000 to 300,000 patients are newly diagnosed with brain metastases each year.[2] This large patient population means brain metastasis is not a niche need, but a question that oncology worldwide must continue to answer. Systemic therapies can help control disease throughout the body, but treatment of intracranial lesions often remains constrained by multiple factors, including the blood-brain barrier, tumor heterogeneity, and the need to preserve neurological function. This is especially true for patients who experience intracranial progression after prior therapy, for whom there remains a need for more treatment options that are validated intracranially while balancing safety and accessibility. Consecutive Clinical Milestones Built on Long-Term Product and Translational Groundwork MT027's recent series of regulatory milestones is no coincidence. It reflects an integrated capability across product, manufacturing, clinical development, and regulatory affairs built around intracranial solid tumors - one that is now advancing from early exploration toward more systematic clinical validation. First, a foundation of clinical data. The company has accumulated sustained clinical experience in local delivery, repeat dosing, and safety monitoring for intracranial solid tumors. Years of clinical experience and data with MT027 have already led to two FDA-cleared Phase 2 programs. Data from an investigator-initiated trial (IIT) of MT026, a program built on the same platform, were published in Nature Communications in 2026: among 5 patients with recurrent high-grade glioma, 1 complete response and 3 partial responses were observed, for an objective response rate (ORR) of 80%, with no treatment-related Grade 3 or higher adverse events. Early clinical data for MT027 in patients with refractory brain metastases from lung cancer were previously presented at the IASLC 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC 2026). Five heavily pretreated patients with no guideline-recommended subsequent treatment options completed treatment; among the 3 evaluable patients, 2 partial responses were observed. The safety profile was favorable, with no Grade 3 or higher adverse events and no graft-versus-host disease (GvHD). These rigorous exploratory clinical studies provide an important basis for the clinical translation of allogeneic, locally delivered CAR-T therapy in intracranial solid tumors. Second, a well-defined manufacturing process. MT027 is manufactured using a fully non-viral gene-editing process - a generational departure from the industry's mainstream lentiviral vector approach - offering potential advantages in product safety, batch-to-batch consistency, and cost control. The manufacturing process was established and locked prior to entering Phase 2 clinical development. Third, leadership measured not only by getting there first, but by advancing systematically. For an innovative cell therapy company, leadership in regulatory progress comes from coordinated advancement across product, manufacturing, clinical development, and regulatory strategy. MT027's consecutive entry into FDA-cleared Phase 2 clinical development demonstrates T-MAXIMUM's ability to translate its prior groundwork into a repeatable and scalable clinical development capability. Management Commentary "Receiving FDA clearance for two consecutive Phase 2 studies of MT027 marks a pivotal step built on our sustained work in intracranial solid tumors. From glioma to brain metastases, we have always let the data speak and put clinical value first. Going forward, we will continue to rigorously evaluate the product's safety and potential clinical value through well-designed clinical studies, steadily advancing product supply, clinical execution, and the generation of key data, as we explore new possibilities for patients who lack effective treatment options." About MT027 MT027 is an investigational, B7-H3-targeted universal (allogeneic) CAR-T cell therapy developed by T-MAXIMUM using a fully non-viral gene-editing process and administered via local intracranial delivery. MT027 has received FDA Orphan Drug Designation and Fast Track Designation and is being evaluated in FDA-cleared Phase 2 studies in recurrent glioblastoma and in brain metastases from lung cancer and breast cancer. About T-MAXIMUM PHARMACEUTICAL T-MAXIMUM PHARMACEUTICAL is a clinical-stage cell therapy company focused on developing universal (allogeneic) CAR-T therapies for intracranial solid tumors with high unmet medical need, including recurrent glioblastoma and brain metastases. Through engineered cell therapies, local delivery strategies, and clinical translation capabilities, the Company is advancing more accessible treatment approaches with the potential to support repeat dosing. Its lead program, MT027, is a B7-H3-targeted universal CAR-T therapy that has received FDA clearance to initiate Phase 2 clinical studies in recurrent glioblastoma and brain metastases. MT027 has also received Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) in high-grade glioma and Fast Track Designation (FTD) for recurrent or progressive glioblastoma. T-MAXIMUM is working to translate its accumulated capabilities in product development, manufacturing, and clinical execution into continued innovation across both primary and metastatic intracranial solid tumors, with the goal of creating new possibilities for patients with limited treatment options. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements, including statements regarding the clinical development, potential therapeutic benefits, manufacturing advantages, and regulatory progress of MT027 and other product candidates. These statements are based on current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties, including those inherent in clinical development, regulatory review, and manufacturing, that could cause actual results to differ materially. Early clinical results from small numbers of patients may not be predictive of results in larger studies. MT027 is an investigational product, and its safety and efficacy have not been established.
